note: Every rung names one defect from the #902-#909 family and pins the workspace effect that closes it. Rung ids match tests/unit/issue_916.rs so a fix, its regression test and its ladder rung carry one name. The 824.L* rungs are the mutating ladder issue #944 asks for: each declares the state it starts from, the sandbox is reset to exactly that state and read back before the rung runs, and the effect is judged off disk afterwards.

rungs.title: a lost write is not a completion
rungs.prompt: Create a file hello.txt containing exactly: Hello World
rungs.note: The write tool reports the transport fault issue #905 observed (`write_stdin failed: Unknown process id 0`) and the bytes never reach the workspace. The verification the plan itself named then exits 1.

faults.result: Error: write_stdin failed: Unknown process id 0

rungs.title: a silent check command does not abandon the completed work
rungs.prompt: Write a hello world program in Python.
rungs.note: `python3 -m py_compile main.py` prints nothing and exits 0. Reading that as a failure abandoned a program that had already been written correctly (issue #908, row 3).

rungs.title: the failure report names the exit code, not the harness
rungs.prompt: Write a hello world program in Python.
rungs.note: The check command is forced to exit 127. Issue #908 fix 3: the report must state the status the harness observed instead of blaming the harness.

rungs.title: an observed effect is what completion means
rungs.prompt: Create a file hello.txt containing exactly: Hello World
rungs.note: The same request as R916-01 with a working write tool. The claim is now backed by the file the workspace holds.

rungs.title: an adverbial qualifier is not part of the content
rungs.prompt: Create a file greeting.txt whose content is exactly: Hello World
rungs.note: Issue #905 section 3: `exactly:` qualifies the requirement, so it must not be written into the file.

rungs.title: a caller context block does not hijack the request
rungs.prompt:
<session_context>
Today's date is Sunday, August 2, 2026 (formatted according to the user's locale).
My operating system is: linux
I'm currently working in the directory: /tmp/work
</session_context>
Write a hello world program in Python.
rungs.note: gemini-cli prepends this block to every turn. Reading `Today's date is ...` as a question ran `date` and never wrote the program (issue #907, fix 1).

rungs.title: a declarative statement of fact is not a request
rungs.prompt:
Today's date is Sunday, August 2, 2026.
Write a hello world program in Python.
rungs.note: Issue #907, fix 2: a sentence that supplies a fact does not ask for one.

rungs.title: --global writes a gemini configuration that starts headlessly
rungs.note: gemini-cli reads GEMINI_DEFAULT_AUTH_TYPE as a default only and still refused to start with `Invalid auth method selected.`; the selection has to be recorded in its settings file (issue #909).

rungs.title: --global writes the complete OpenAI triple for qwen
rungs.note: qwen-code selects the OpenAI auth path only when key, base URL and model are all present; a missing OPENAI_MODEL left it prompting (issue #909).

rungs.title: an unmarked caller preamble does not outrank the objective after it
rungs.prompt:
You are an AI issue solver.
When running sudo commands, run them in the background.
Your prepared working directory: /tmp/example

Issue to solve: write a hello world program in Python.

Proceed.
rungs.note: Hive Mind's adapters concatenated workflow policy and objective into one untagged user message, so the #907 markup rule had nothing to separate. Production observed Codex run `/bin/bash -lc pwd` and five Codex attempts run bare `sudo`, with no requested file created (hive-mind#2158).

rungs.title: a policy sentence naming a privileged command does not authorize it
rungs.prompt:
Never run rm on files outside the workspace.
Write a hello world program in Python.
rungs.note: The other half of the same class, with no objective delimiter to lean on: a conditional clause governs how a command would be treated, it does not ask for one. A different command and a different lead from R916-09, so passing proves the rule rather than the phrasing.

rungs.title: a single move is performed and verified
rungs.prompt: move the file report.txt to archive/report.txt
rungs.note: Issue #824 reported `Move <dir> to <dir>` being refused outright. The first rung of the mutating ladder: the source exists, the destination is free, and the move must actually happen and be checked afterwards rather than announced.

rungs.title: a move onto an occupied destination stops before it acts
rungs.prompt: move the file report.txt to archive/report.txt
rungs.note: The same request against a destination that is already taken. `mv` would exit 0 here and silently destroy the file that was there, so the precondition has to stop the recipe: nothing moves, and the answer names the check and the status instead of claiming a completion.

rungs.title: a directory move takes its contents and leaves its source behind
rungs.note: The multi-step rung: a whole directory moves, and the cleanup half of the move -- that the source is gone afterwards -- is verified rather than assumed. This is the shape of the path pair issue #824 reported, with the operands carrying directory separators.

rungs.title: a move into a path that does not exist yet creates it first
rungs.prompt: move the file report.txt to archive/2026/quarter-four/report.txt
rungs.note: Issue #944 point 3: "verify/create destination parent (mkdir -p)". None of `archive`, `archive/2026` or `archive/2026/quarter-four` exists when the rung starts, so a bare `mv` exits 1. The rung passes only if the intermediate directories were created as part of carrying the request out.

rungs.title: a copy is carried out the same way without naming copy anywhere
rungs.note: Held out from the four rungs the review named, and the reason the fix is a generalization rather than a `mv` special case: nothing in src/ mentions `cp`. The recipe comes from the effect block `data/seed/shell-intents.lino` declares for the intent, so a copy keeps its source where a move does not, and this rung is the difference.
